variants.name: Current architecture
variants.summary: Service level: browser application modules. Follow linked subjects for related levels.

nodes.name: Browser client
nodes.responsibility: The viewer: it owns the camera, the active view, the walkthrough position and what somebody picked out, and writes nothing
nodes.description: ADR 0023. Board content lives here only as a read-only cache of what the server said, read again when the server announces a new version. A person's one control over a board is taking back somebody else's claim.

nodes.name: Application composition
nodes.responsibility: Connects pane and feature owners
nodes.description: Mounts one pane per pane id (its session and its stage together, ApplicationPane), composes the agent's owners over the focused pane's transport, keeps voice on the pane it was started for, and connects routing, the catalog, notices, settings, narration, subtitles and a recording page. It holds no board content.

nodes.name: Semantic viewer
nodes.responsibility: Reads and explores rendered boards
nodes.description: Reads the board document from the server and draws its picture in this page (or asks the server's render route when the page runs no renderer). Owns only camera, selection, view, variant, walkthrough position and drill-down trail, and writes nothing (ADR 0023).

nodes.name: Pane session
nodes.responsibility: Keeps each pane in server contact
nodes.description: Owns the pane's socket and its generations, registration and pane reports, board news, taking back a claim, opening code, and the workbench transport each socket generation carries.

nodes.name: Workspace routing
nodes.responsibility: Restores pane display intent
nodes.description: One TanStack Router route at /, whose search parameters paneA, paneB and pane are the workspace. The address follows what the panes report; on a first load and on Back or Forward it leads, restoring through the workspace port with the same command the navigator runs. It is never board authority.

nodes.name: Board catalog
nodes.responsibility: Lists boards available to open
nodes.description: Owns the tab's query cache and the live panes' inventory query, composes that inventory with the viewer's board listing into what the navigator shows, and holds the invalidations the application calls when pane news says a board moved.

nodes.name: Workbench client
nodes.responsibility: The agent bar under the panes and the conversation beside them: the agent's state and its one action, Talk, the composer, and the conversation with its work, plans and approvals
nodes.description: Reads one AgentView and acts through one AgentActions, both composed by the application over the agent setup, the focused pane's controllers and the voice session.

nodes.name: Voice session
nodes.responsibility: The live voice this tab holds for one pane: availability, start and stop, mute, recovery
nodes.description: Made by the application's VoiceStore for the pane voice runs for. The peer connection and the audio element belong to that pane's media owner (codex-workbench-media), negotiated over the pane's workbench transport.

nodes.name: Code target
nodes.responsibility: Opens the code a subject is bound to
nodes.description: Sends the board and the subject's id to the Archboard server, which owns the binding, the opener and the checkout registry, and opens the code at the branch or commit the binding pins. The browser never reads a local path. Also reads, tests and saves the opener settings.

nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: Owns every board and answers every read

nodes.name: Shell
nodes.responsibility: The desktop frame: header, navigator, the panes, the agent bar under them and the conversation panel beside them

nodes.name: Browser renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws a board in this tab: the tab's own canvas for measuring, a worker pool for the layout

nodes.name: Server requests
nodes.responsibility: The one way this tab speaks JSON to the Archboard server

nodes.name: Agent setup
nodes.responsibility: Talking needs no setup: a message or Talk is held and carried through sign-in, Codex starting and the conversation's creation
nodes.description: One setup for the whole server, outliving focus. Each held message says what it waits on; a failure stays on it with the reason, and nothing is retried behind the user's back. nodes.name: Workbench transport
nodes.responsibility: The agent's channel on one pane socket: the server's agent state in, the controllers' commands out

nodes.name: Walkthrough recording

nodes.name: Frame clock
nodes.responsibility: The one clock that glides, picture transitions and subtitle lingers read: the browser's own on a live page, a stepped one on a replay

It pauses and stands every Web Animation, CSS transition and SMIL root at the frame's time, and records a violation for an animation on a timeline it cannot stand. A lint rule keeps the viewer and the subtitles on it.

It pauses and stands every Web Animation and CSS transition at the frame's time, a picture's traffic at where its picture's clock stands, and records a violation for an animation on a timeline it cannot stand. A lint rule keeps the viewer and the subtitles on it.

walkthroughs.name: Reading a board in the browser

beats.heading: Restore the workspace
beats.body: Routing reads the address and restores it through the workspace port: application composition opens each board in its pane with the same command the navigator runs, and writes the address only once the pane reports its new board.

beats.heading: Read the board, draw it here
beats.body: The semantic viewer reads the board document from the server and the browser renderer draws it in this tab. The viewer owns camera, selection, views, variants, walkthroughs and drill-down only, and writes nothing.

beats.heading: Carry the active context
beats.body: The pane socket brings a board's new version to the viewer and carries the workbench transport. The pane reports what is on screen, and opens bound code through the code target.

beats.heading: Talk without setup
beats.body: A message, Talk or Narrate goes to the agent setup, which carries it through sign-in, Codex starting and the creation of the tab's conversation, then delivers it or starts voice for the focused pane. Each tab has its own conversation and voice, so two tabs can talk at the same time. A reload keeps the conversation. The voice's words appear as subtitles over that pane.

beats.heading: Record a walkthrough
beats.body: A page opened to record asks for voice as a recording and moves its one pane a step at a time as the voice paces it. It keeps the talk: the voice's sound, and each step and subtitle line on the same clock. It captures no picture. The page is its own tab session, so voice that is live in another tab does not refuse it. The voice is never played aloud.

beats.heading: Replay a talk frame by frame
beats.body: A page opened to replay draws a recorded talk again. It mounts the recording's stage, the viewer and the subtitles, with no workbench and no socket, and reads the board only from the talk. Every glide, picture transition and subtitle linger reads the frame clock, which the replay steps 1/30 s at a time.

variants.name: TASK-391
variants.summary: Service level: browser application modules. Follow linked subjects for related levels.

nodes.name: Browser client
nodes.responsibility: The viewer: it owns the camera, the active view, the walkthrough position and what somebody picked out, and writes nothing
nodes.description: ADR 0023. Board content lives here only as a read-only cache of what the server said, read again when the server announces a new version. A person's one control over a board is taking back somebody else's claim.

nodes.name: Application composition
nodes.responsibility: Connects pane and feature owners
nodes.description: Mounts one pane per pane id (its session and its stage together, ApplicationPane), composes the agent's owners over the focused pane's transport, keeps voice on the pane it was started for, and connects routing, the catalog, notices, settings, narration, subtitles and a recording page. Both panes carry the tab's session, so the agent is the same whichever pane has focus. It holds no board content.

nodes.name: Semantic viewer
nodes.responsibility: Reads and explores rendered boards
nodes.description: Reads the board document from the server, or from the talk on a replay, and draws its picture in this page (or asks the server's render route when the page runs no renderer). Owns only camera, selection, view, variant, walkthrough position and drill-down trail, and writes nothing (ADR 0023).

nodes.name: Pane session
nodes.responsibility: Keeps each pane in server contact
nodes.description: Owns the pane's socket and its generations, registration and pane reports, board news, taking back a claim, opening code, and the workbench transport each socket generation carries. Every socket names the tab session, so the server knows which panes share a conversation.

nodes.name: Workspace routing
nodes.responsibility: Restores pane display intent
nodes.description: One TanStack Router route at /, whose search parameters paneA, paneB and pane are the workspace. The address follows what the panes report; on a first load and on Back or Forward it leads, restoring through the workspace port with the same command the navigator runs. It is never board authority.

nodes.name: Board catalog
nodes.responsibility: Lists boards available to open
nodes.description: Owns the tab's query cache and the live panes' inventory query, composes that inventory with the viewer's board listing into what the navigator shows, and holds the invalidations the application calls when pane news says a board moved.

nodes.name: Workbench client
nodes.description: Reads one AgentView and acts through one AgentActions, both composed by the application over the agent setup, the focused pane's controllers and the voice session. While the person wants subtitles it also draws the voice box over the voice's pane, which carries the voice the dock otherwise shows; the dock hands the voice over only to a box that the orb's stage says is on the page.

nodes.name: Voice session
nodes.responsibility: The live voice this tab holds for one pane: availability, start and stop, mute, recovery
nodes.description: Made by the application's VoiceStore for the pane voice runs for. The peer connection and the audio element belong to that pane's media owner (codex-workbench-media), negotiated over the pane's workbench transport.

nodes.name: Code target
nodes.responsibility: Opens the code a subject is bound to
nodes.description: Sends the board and the subject's id to the Archboard server, which owns the binding, the opener and the checkout registry, and opens the code at the branch or commit the binding pins. The browser never reads a local path. Also reads, tests and saves the opener settings.

nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: Owns every board and answers every read

nodes.name: Shell
nodes.responsibility: The desktop frame: header, navigator, the panes, the agent bar under them and the conversation panel beside them

nodes.name: Browser renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws a board in this tab: the tab's own canvas for measuring, a worker pool for the layout

nodes.name: Server requests
nodes.responsibility: The one way this tab speaks JSON to the Archboard server

nodes.name: Agent setup
nodes.responsibility: Talking needs no setup: a message or Talk is held and carried through sign-in, Codex starting and the creation of the tab's conversation
nodes.description: One setup for the tab, outliving focus: both panes share the tab's conversation. Each held message says what it waits on. A failure stays on it with the reason, and nothing is retried behind the user's back. It speaks through ports the application wires to the focused pane's thread link, composer and voice session.

nodes.name: Workbench transport
nodes.responsibility: The agent's channel on one pane socket: the server's agent state in, the controllers' commands out

nodes.name: Voice subtitles
nodes.responsibility: The voice's words, faded in one at a time over the pane it runs for, measured into two lines
nodes.description: Cut into cues from the transcript on the pane's transport, or from a talk's lines on a replay; each word fades in, a cue gives way to the next without a cut, and a subtitle that stops growing lingers on the frame clock, then fades out. A person can turn them off, which moves the voice from the box that carries it back to the dock; a recording always has them.

nodes.name: Walkthrough recording
nodes.responsibility: A page recording one walkthrough's talk: it moves the pane a step at a time as the voice paces it, and keeps the voice and each step and subtitle line on one clock
nodes.description: Asked for by the page's address. The page shows the one pane (RecordingStage) instead of the shell and publishes its contract on the window for the recorder that drives it (drawn on Board rasterizer). The page is its own tab session, so voice that is live in another tab does not refuse it. The voice's audio element is muted, so nobody hears it, and its stream is tapped through Web Audio. The talk's lines are the voice's own lines of the transcript on the pane's transport, and its drawn versions are what the pane reports. The page captures no picture: the replay draws every frame again from the talk.

nodes.name: Tab session
nodes.responsibility: The tab's own id, kept in sessionStorage: a reload keeps it, and a new tab or window mints another
nodes.description: Both panes of a tab send it on their sockets, so they share one conversation and one voice. The server never takes a thread id from the browser. A duplicated tab copies the id and shares the conversation.

nodes.name: Walkthrough replay
nodes.responsibility: A page drawing a recorded talk again, one frame at a time: the recording's pane and subtitles, fed from the talk, on a stepped clock
nodes.description: Asked for by ?replay=1, and mounted by the entry point in place of the application, so it has no workbench, no pane session and no socket, and no Codex is involved. It publishes load(talk) and frame(n) on the window for the renderer that drives it (drawn on Board rasterizer). It reads the board and the policy only from the talk, and a read of any other board fails the render.

nodes.name: Frame clock
nodes.responsibility: The one clock that glides, picture transitions and subtitle lingers read: the browser's own on a live page, a stepped one on a replay
nodes.description: A replay swaps it once, before it mounts anything. Its stepped clock runs frame callbacks and timers at their due times, and takes over the browser's own requestAnimationFrame, so a library's frames run on it too. It pauses and stands every Web Animation and CSS transition at the frame's time, a picture's traffic at where its picture's clock stands, and records a violation for an animation on a timeline it cannot stand. A lint rule keeps the viewer and the subtitles on it.

nodes.name: Voice orb
nodes.description: The canvas is made once and moved, never remounted, so the light and the last second of level it has drawn go with it. The dock offers its circle as one home and the voice box offers a socket as the other; the stage flies the orb over the page between them, meets a socket where it is as it moves, turns a flight round from where the orb is, and cuts when motion is not wanted or a home is not on screen. It says whether a home is on the page, so a surface gives the voice up only to a home that is there.
